subject: Onboarding sprint: GPU sourcing playbook & cloud contingency
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie King <sophie@atlasml.com>, sales@oakchips.com, partners@novasilicon.com
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Onboarding sprint: GPU sourcing playbook & cloud contingency

Hi Sophie and team,

Thanks again for the sync yesterday. As discussed, AtlasML's Q3 onboarding window is narrow and we need a concrete sourcing/playbook for the Dedicated capacity portion of the deal (DEAL-8342). To move your procurement board on Apr 20 we need:

- OEM lead times and firm ETA ranges (per SKU)
- Any minimum order/commit terms that would affect our reserved-capacity proposals
- Short-term cloud contingency options (region: eu-central) while hardware arrives

Attached is our initial requirements worksheet (sourcing_requirements_v1.xlsx) with target throughput, preferred SKUs, and an estimated ramp profile. Can OakChips and NovaSilicon confirm lead times by EOD Fri so we can fold numbers into the mutual action plan?

We'd like to keep next steps simple: if OEM lead time >10 weeks, we trigger the cloud contingency (reserve short-term Dedicated nodes) and map cost delta. If <=10 weeks we prioritize OEM; if mixed SKUs we do a hybrid.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.ai
[Attachment: sourcing_requirements_v1.xlsx]

---
From: Sophie King <sophie@atlasml.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 11:05:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding sprint: GPU sourcing playbook & cloud contingency

Monica / Aditya,

Thanks — this is super helpful. Procurement calendar attached (atlas_procurement_calendar.pdf). Quick notes from our side:

- Procurement review is on Apr 20 and legal sign-off targeted Apr 27.
- Our board prefers OEM-first for budget reasons but will accept a hybrid if we can demonstrate cost/time tradeoffs.
- Short-term cloud reservations are acceptable for up to 12 weeks; they'd need clear rollback terms.

Could Aditya provide a high-level landed cost and a 0/1/2 SKU split estimate for the hybrid scenario by EOD Fri? That will let us present an apples-to-apples comparison.

Best,
Sophie King
Procurement Lead, AtlasML
sophie@atlasml.com
[Attachment: atlas_procurement_calendar.pdf]

---
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Sophie King <sophie@atlasml.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 08:30:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding sprint: GPU sourcing playbook & cloud contingency

Sophie / Monica — per our vendor checks overnight I pulled preliminary numbers into OEM_quote_summary.pdf. Highlights:

- OakChips: SKU OC-80 (preferred) lead time 12–14 weeks, MOQ 8 units; quoted price €58k/unit ex-VAT; partial shipments allowed but incur handling fee.
- NovaSilicon: SKU NS-XL lead time 8–10 weeks, MOQ 4 units; quoted price €66k/unit ex-VAT; can prioritize EU shipments for slight premium.
- If we do hybrid (mix OC-80 + NS-XL) we can meet target throughput sooner but at ~6–9% higher total HW cost due to NS premium and cross-shipping fees.

I've attached a one-pager summary and a simple cost matrix. If Sophie confirms which SKUs AtlasML prefers (cost-sensitive vs. time-sensitive), we can model two firm options for the board: OEM-first (Nova heavy) vs Hybrid (initial Nova bridged with Oak later).

Action items I propose:
1) OakChips to confirm whether MOQ is flexible and earliest partial shipment date (Oak please reply in-thread)
2) NovaSilicon to confirm expedited EU fulfillment delta for NS-XL (partners@novasilicon.com)
3) Marcus to run the Reserved-Node delta estimate for 12 weeks in eu-central (Marcus, can you post numbers by Mon morning?)

Thanks,
Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai
[Attachment: OEM_quote_summary.pdf]

---
From: OakChips Sales <sales@oakchips.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Sophie King <sophie@atlasml.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 13:22:05 +0100
Subject: Re: Onboarding sprint: GPU sourcing playbook & cloud contingency

Hi all,

Thanks for the inquiry. Confirming the OC-80 lead time is currently 12–14 weeks from PO acceptance. A few clarifications:

- MOQ of 8 units is firm for standard lead time; we can offer partial shipment options at week 10 for up to 50% of the order, subject to a €5k handling fee per partial shipment.
- We can commit to EU customs pre-clearance to shave ~4 business days if paperwork is prepared at PO time.
- Price hold: quoted pricing valid for 21 days.

If you want to accelerate beyond partial shipments, we can provide a shortage allocation at premium pricing; let's discuss on a call — available Mon 05 Apr 09:00–11:00 CET.

Regards,
Elena Markovic
Regional Sales Manager, OakChips
sales@oakchips.com
[Attachment: OakChips_OC-80_term_sheet.pdf (PDF stub)]

---
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sophie King <sophie@atlasml.com>, sales@oakchips.com, partners@novasilicon.com, cloudops@eucentral.cloud
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding sprint: GPU sourcing playbook & cloud contingency

Team — summary and immediate asks (condensed for exec review):

Summary:
- NovaSilicon can hit ~8–10 week lead time (best path to meet Apr 20 procurement board) but at ~€8k/unit premium vs OakChips.
- OakChips lead time 12–14 weeks, MOQ constraints but partial shipment option exists (fee applies).
- Hybrid gives fastest ramp but increases HW cost by ~6–9% and adds logistics complexity.

Immediate asks (owners & deadlines):
- Marcus: run Reserved-Node delta for 12 weeks in eu-central (include networking, egress estimate) — due Mon 2027-04-05 09:00 CET.
- Aditya: produce 2 slide comparison for board (OEM-first Nova vs Hybrid) with landed cost and TCO delta — due Mon 2027-04-05 12:00 CET.
- Priyom: draft contingency contract language for short-term reserved nodes (rollback window, termination, credits) — due Tue 2027-04-06 EOD.
- OakChips / NovaSilicon: confirm any flexibility on MOQ / partial shipments and expedited EU fulfillment by EOD Mon.

Risks & mitigations:
- If Nova fails to lock expedited EU fulfillment, we flip to hybrid + immediate short-term reserved capacity. Marcus, please include a time-to-switch operational checklist.

Sophie — once we have Marcus/Aditya/Priyom numbers on Monday we can produce a short one-page decision brief for your procurement board on Apr 20.

Thanks everyone — keeping this in my inbox so I can escalate if we miss the Monday ask.

Monica Patel
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.ai
[Attachment: none]
